value.body: Tests raw materials, in-process samples and finished products in a chemical lab using standard methods, and records the results. Lab chemists work in pharmaceutical, chemical, food, cement, paint and water-testing industries, and in independent testing labs. A day involves preparing samples, running instruments and titrations, and keeping records that meet quality and regulatory requirements.

items.label: Typical entry
items.note: An M.Sc is common for QA and analytical R&D roles

items.label: Common instruments
items.value: HPLC, GC, UV-Vis, FTIR, pH meters and titration setups

items.label: Systems followed
items.value: Good laboratory practice, ISO/IEC 17025 (NABL), GMP in pharma

items.label: NABL-accredited testing labs
items.note: Testing labs only; calibration and medical labs are counted separately
items.source: NABL directory of accredited testing laboratories, as reported

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers start as trainee or QC chemists in manufacturing units or NABL-accredited testing labs, often through walk-in drives in industrial areas. Lab practicals, familiarity with instruments and careful documentation are what interviews check. An M.Sc in Chemistry widens options into QA, analytical R&D and method development.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Wet chemistry — titration and sample preparation

value.title: At a glance
items: Shift work is common in plant QC labs.
Growth path: chemist → senior chemist → QC/QA officer → lab in-charge.
Pharma QC roles involve heavy documentation and regular audits.
